findings.note: mustResultFile drops ParseResult's ignore reason: `if _, _, err := reviewmanifest.ParseResult(data); err != nil` (cmd/metareview/main.go:630) treats only a JSON unmarshal failure as invalid. reviewmanifest.ParseResult (internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:148-158) returns (zero, reason, nil) for a file over MaxResultBytes and (zero, "", nil) for any well-formed JSON object, so an oversized result file, an empty {}, a literal null, or a JSON document of a completely different schema passes the CLI guard with exit 0. The function's own doc comment and docs/tasks/pr-b-shard-ingestion.md both claim a bad --shard-result exits 2 with nothing written; that holds only for non-JSON input. Impact is limited to diagnosability, not gate correctness: shardpack.Discover (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:332-339) re-parses and files the same file under Ignored with the reason, which reaches the review log via IgnoredResults, and the shard simply stays uncovered, so the gate fails closed.

findings.note: handleOverride hand-rolls flag parsing instead of reusing flagValue, so it is inconsistent with every other flag in the binary. `metareview override request ID --reason` with no value silently leaves reason empty (the `if i+1 < len(args)` guard has no else) and surfaces as the generic 'needs a reason of at least 12 characters' on exit 1, where flagValue (cmd/metareview/main.go:467-473) would print 'Missing value for --reason' and exit 2. Worse, `--reason --by dave` is accepted with the literal string '--by' as the recorded reason, because unlike flagValue this parser does not reject a value beginning with '--'. The recorded reason is audit data that a human later reads to judge an exception, so a silently captured flag name is a bad audit row.

findings.note: A granted override permanently silences its fingerprint for that target, with no expiry and no re-open on a changed git head. activeExisting was widened from `record.Status == "open"` to `record.Status != "fixed"` (internal/findings/findings.go:154), so once a record reaches StatusOverridden the same fingerprint is never re-created on any later run for the same target; Blocks (internal/findings/override.go:53) excludes it, and the activeCurrent filter still requires status==open, so the finding also disappears from Result.Findings and therefore from the review log body. That is defensible as the point of an override, but nothing in the diff bounds it to the head or the run that was excepted, and there is no withdraw command, so an acknowledged exception outlives the code it was granted against. Worth an explicit decision (and a doc line) rather than an emergent consequence of the != "fixed" widening.
